briefingRaw.roleSummary:
Highlights
  • Supplier Manager (ORA_POZ_SUPPLIER_MANAGER_ABSTRACT) grants access to a wide range of functionalities related to supplier management and collaboration. It allows users to view and manage supplier qualifications, assessments, and match results. The privilege enables updates to supplier contacts, profiles, and business relationships. Additionally, it provides access to collaboration messaging, including viewing and managing messages, documents, and setup data. also facilitates the management of external partners, trading partners, and service providers. Users can update tax profiles, fiscal classifications, and location of final discharge. The privilege grants access to various work areas, such as suppliers and collaboration messaging, and allows the monitoring and reprocessing of messages. Furthermore, it enables the management of file import and export, collaboration message logging, and collaboration document data access. With this privilege, users can also search and merge suppliers, as well as manage payment instrument assignments and external payee payment details.

briefingRaw.roleUsage:
The Supplier Manager role includes 138 privileges, which can be summarized into the following functional categories


1. Supplier Management: Involves the comprehensive management of suppliers, encompassing their registration, qualification, and assessment processes. This cluster includes privileges related to maintaining and updating supplier profiles, business relationships, and transaction tax information. It also covers the ability to search and view supplier registration requests, qualifications, and assessments. Additionally, it enables the management of supplier contacts, attachments, and site information, as well as the ability to process and retransmit collaboration messages related to suppliers.

2. Collaboration Messaging: Focuses on the management and configuration of collaboration messaging systems. This cluster includes privileges related to setting up and validating collaboration messaging setup, as well as managing collaboration message logging, history, and domain value maps. It also enables users to view and process collaboration messages, reprocess failed messages, and monitor collaboration messaging work areas. Additionally, it provides access to manage collaboration document data access for users and collaboration message definitions.

3. Tax and Fiscal Management: Pertains to the management of tax-related information and fiscal classifications. This cluster includes privileges related to maintaining and updating tax profiles for third parties and third-party sites, as well as managing tax fiscal classification import and export services. It also enables users to create, view, and update party fiscal classifications and third-party tax profiles. Additionally, it provides access to manage external partner message and trading partners by web service.

4. File and Data Management: Includes the management and import/export of files and data. This cluster includes privileges related to setting up and managing file import and export activities, as well as loading interface files for import and transferring files. It also enables users to set up CRM objects for export and manage customer account collaboration configuration. Additionally, it provides access to manage message delivery endpoints and transformation configurations.

5. Web Service Management: Contains privileges related to managing and accessing various aspects of web services. This cluster includes privileges for managing trading partners, B2B locations, and certificates by web service. It also enables users to manage service providers and collaboration messaging history by web service. Additionally, it provides access to view and manage collaboration message definitions and trading partners by web service.

6. Miscellaneous: Contains items that do not belong to any specific group. This cluster includes privileges related to running background scheduler processes, maintaining reports and analytics, and managing scheduled job definitions. It also enables users to access the suppliers work area overview and monitor collaboration messaging. Additionally, it provides access to use REST services for guided journeys and responses, as well as managing external payee payment details and account numbers by web service.

briefingRaw.roleUsage:
The Supplier Manager role includes 138 privileges, which can be summarized into the following functional categories


1. Supplier Management: Involves the comprehensive management of suppliers, encompassing their registration, qualification, and assessment processes. This cluster includes privileges related to maintaining and updating supplier profiles, business relationships, and transaction tax information. It also covers the ability to search and view supplier registration requests, qualifications, and assessments. Additionally, it enables the management of supplier contacts, attachments, and site information, as well as the ability to process and retransmit collaboration messages related to suppliers.

2. Collaboration Messaging: Focuses on the management and configuration of collaboration messaging systems. This cluster includes privileges related to setting up and validating collaboration messaging setup, as well as managing collaboration message logging, history, and domain value maps. It also enables users to view and process collaboration messages, reprocess failed messages, and monitor collaboration messaging work areas. Additionally, it provides access to manage collaboration document data access for users and collaboration message definitions.

3. Tax and Fiscal Management: Pertains to the management of tax-related information and fiscal classifications. This cluster includes privileges related to maintaining and updating tax profiles for third parties and third-party sites, as well as managing tax fiscal classification import and export services. It also enables users to create, view, and update party fiscal classifications and third-party tax profiles. Additionally, it provides access to manage external partner message and trading partners by web service.

4. File and Data Management: Includes the management and import/export of files and data. This cluster includes privileges related to setting up and managing file import and export activities, as well as loading interface files for import and transferring files. It also enables users to set up CRM objects for export and manage customer account collaboration configuration. Additionally, it provides access to manage message delivery endpoints and transformation configurations.

5. Web Service Management: Contains privileges related to managing and accessing various aspects of web services. This cluster includes privileges for managing trading partners, B2B locations, and certificates by web service. It also enables users to manage service providers and collaboration messaging history by web service. Additionally, it provides access to view and manage collaboration message definitions and trading partners by web service.

6. Miscellaneous: Contains items that do not belong to any specific group. This cluster includes privileges related to running background scheduler processes, maintaining reports and analytics, and managing scheduled job definitions. It also enables users to access the suppliers work area overview and monitor collaboration messaging. Additionally, it provides access to use REST services for guided journeys and responses, as well as managing external payee payment details and account numbers by web service.

Highlights
  • Supplier Manager (ORA_POZ_SUPPLIER_MANAGER_ABSTRACT) grants access to a wide range of functionalities related to supplier management and collaboration. It allows users to view and manage supplier qualifications, assessments, and match results. The privilege enables updates to supplier contacts, profiles, and business relationships. Additionally, it provides access to collaboration messaging, including viewing and managing messages, documents, and setup data. also facilitates the management of external partners, trading partners, and service providers. Users can update tax profiles, fiscal classifications, and location of final discharge. The privilege grants access to various work areas, such as suppliers and collaboration messaging, and allows the monitoring and reprocessing of messages. Furthermore, it enables the management of file import and export, collaboration message logging, and collaboration document data access. With this privilege, users can also search and merge suppliers, as well as manage payment instrument assignments and external payee payment details.
